blocks.text: Absalom first builds popular support by presenting himself as an accessible source of justice. He then declares himself king at Hebron, and the growing conspiracy forces David to leave Jerusalem. The remainder of the chapter follows David’s departure and his arrangements for receiving information from the city.

Second Samuel moves from David’s rise and the consolidation of his kingdom into royal abuse, violence within his household, rebellion, and grief. Absalom’s revolt belongs to this later movement of the book, where David’s reign is increasingly marked by conflict and loss.
